items.title: Common types of programming errors and bugs

source_refs.note: Unnumbered topic Common types of programming errors and bugs as printed (PDF 64-65, printed 60-61); its own lesson since 2026-10-29 (one lesson per book heading), moved from the topic 5.2.1 lesson.

blocks.text: Syntax errors occur when code does not follow language rules. Logic errors happen when the program produces incorrect results. Runtime errors appear while the program is running. Other common bugs include data errors and resource leaks. Identifying these errors is key to building stable applications (as shown in Figure 5.1).

blocks.alt: Types of Program Errors, three panels. Logic Error: length = 5, width = 3, area = length + width (# Incorrect logic), print(area) gives 8, an incorrect result; the program runs but the formula is wrong; Correct logic: area = length * width, output 15. Runtime Error: a = 10, b = 0, result = a / b gives ZeroDivisionError: division by zero; the program stops during execution. Syntax Error: if x > 5 without a colon gives SyntaxError: invalid syntax; Correct syntax: if x > 5:.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.1: Example showing logic error, runtime error and syntax error (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.1).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 5.1 repeats '# Output: 8 (incorrect result)' under the corrected formula area = length * width; the correct output is 15, as drawn above.
